sources.entry: XBackBone - Simple, fast and lightweight file manager with instant sharing tools integration, like ShareX. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: XBackBone is a self-hosted, lightweight file and media sharing platform with first-class ShareX support, short share links, and multi-user management.
summary.what_it_does: It lets users upload images, GIFs, video, audio, PDFs, code and arbitrary files, then share them through short links with social embeds. The README lists one-click uploader configs for ShareX, ScreenCloud, ishare, Spectacle (KDE), the macOS Share sheet, Xerahs and a CLI script, pre-filled with the instance URL and a personal token. Storage backends include local disk, Amazon S3 (and S3-compatible), FTP and SFTP. It supports per-resource visibility, optional password protection and expiration, and content-addressed de-duplication. It also provides a REST API with token auth and OpenAPI docs, two-factor (TOTP) and passkey (WebAuthn) login, admin roles, per-user disk quotas, an activity log, feature flags, a guided web installer, in-app updates, and legacy XBackBone import.
use_cases: share screenshots and files via short links
personal file and media sharing server
upload files from ScreenCloud or Spectacle
migrate from a legacy XBackBone instance
how_to_run: Read the documentation for installation, configuration and usage (the README does not list commands).
notable: Monorepo split: core/ holds the application as a Composer package, app/ is a thin skeleton, so upgrades are done by changing the required core version
Built-in ShareX and other uploader config generator pre-filled with instance URL and token
Content-addressed storage that de-duplicates uploads by fingerprint
Guided browser installer and in-app updates without shell access
Legacy XBackBone import with old links redirected
caveats: The README says this is a rebuilt next-generation version; details of stability are not stated
Full setup and configuration are only referred to the external documentation
Development setup is described in core/README.md, which was not provided
